Their rebuilding period was brief, however, as they drafted [Rick Barry](/wiki/Rick_Barry "Rick Barry") four months after the trade. Barry, along with [Jamaal Wilkes](/wiki/Jamaal_Wilkes "Jamaal Wilkes"), powered the Warriors to their third championship in [1975](/wiki/1975_NBA_Finals "1975 NBA Finals"), widely considered one of the biggest upsets in NBA history.

The team struggled in the 1980s, then became playoff regulars at the turn of the decade with stars [Tim Hardaway](/wiki/Tim_Hardaway "Tim Hardaway"), [Mitch Richmond](/wiki/Mitch_Richmond "Mitch Richmond"), and [Chris Mullin](/wiki/Chris_Mullin "Chris Mullin"), nicknamed "[Run TMC](/wiki/Run_TMC "Run TMC")". The [modern history period](/wiki/Modern_era "Modern era") of South Asia, that is the 16th century onwards, witnessed the establishment of the Mughal Empire, with Sunni Islam theology. The first ruler was Babur had [Turco-Mongol roots](/wiki/Turco-Mongol_tradition "Turco-Mongol tradition") and his realm included the northwestern and [Indo-Gangetic Plain](/wiki/Indo-Gangetic_Plain "Indo-Gangetic Plain") regions of South Asia. Several regions of South Asia were largely under [Hindu kings](/wiki/Hindu_king "Hindu king") such as those of the Vijayanagara Empire and the [Kingdom of Mewar](/wiki/Kingdom_of_Mewar "Kingdom of Mewar").[[135]](#cite_note-142) Parts of modern [Telangana](/wiki/Telangana "Telangana") and [Andhra Pradesh](/wiki/Andhra_Pradesh "Andhra Pradesh") were under local Muslim rulers, the Deccan Sutanates.

The Mughal Empire continued its wars of expansion after Babur's death. With the fall of the Rajput kingdoms and Vijayanagara, its boundaries encompassed almost the entirety of the Indian subcontinent.[[136]](#cite_note-borocz-143) The Mughal Empire was marked by a period of artistic exchanges and a Central Asian and South Asian architecture synthesis, with remarkable buildings such as the [Taj Mahal](/wiki/Taj_Mahal "Taj Mahal").[[137]](#cite_note-144)[[138]](#cite_note-FOOTNOTEMaddison2003259–261-145)[[139]](#cite_note-harrison-146)
